title: Canonical finite-algebra completion and actual CRT/Dedekind local branches
component_status: Five production leaves and 35 examples compiled; six declaration lint checks, style and standard-three-axiom production audit passed. Final registration and aggregate registered-tree checks remain integrator work.
source_scope: Nine source leaves are manifest-confirmed original-301 members. The endpoint chain is migrated; arbitrary-module ScalarExtension and general monotone reindexing are not claimed. Their ring/positive-power specializations use native suppliers. Old inverse-limit helper implementations are not copied.
excluded_claims: Fraction-field, Milnor norm or residue theorem
Formal smoothness, henselization or Nisnevich theorem
snapshot_method: Actual final compiled source copies, native traces and olean hashes captured before integrator handoff; no reconstruction by removing registration annotations. Source timestamps precede successful olean timestamps. Trace source hash and full dependency trace preserved.
scope: R : Type u and S : Type v are commutative rings with Algebra R S; the canonical tensor map exists for every ideal without finiteness, Noetherianity, flatness or torsion-freeness. It is an equivalence for Noetherian R and Module.Finite R S, also over completion I R with the action from completionMap itself.

Finite pairwise comaximal ideal families over arbitrary commutative rings have actual CRT completion products. Positive-power comparison requires e > 0. Maximal localization may use any selected localization in an independent universe; no Noetherian or domain assumption.

Semilocal branches require the displayed product of positive powers of pairwise comaximal maximal ideals. All forward coordinates equal the original canonical completion maps and retain same-level quotient evaluations, including n = 0.
Dedekind branches are the actual normalized-factor support and multiplicities. Only I != 0 is required; I = top and the empty branch product remain valid.

For finite Dedekind S over Noetherian R, the tensor product is the full actual branch product when I.map(algebraMap R S) != 0. Canonical completed-base action, scalar tower and every-branch finiteness are proved. The action itself does not need Noetherianity, finiteness or a nonzero-ideal assumption.
tests: 35 examples: independent universes, canonical map/generator laws, five explicit level-zero checks, positive powers, an empty-index unit-ideal product, singleton exponent two, actual non-domain Z x Z coordinate CRT, arbitrary quotient algebras, canonical base action without finiteness/Noetherianity/nonzero-ideal assumptions.
